text: Why is special relativity widely thought to threaten presentism?
choices: Because it entails that only the present moment exists, which presentists deny.
Because time dilation proves that clocks in motion objectively run fast rather than slow.
Because the relativity of simultaneity denies any objectively privileged, frame-independent present, whereas presentism requires a unique objective present.
Because it shows directly that past and future events do not exist.
explanation: Special relativity makes simultaneity frame-relative with no physically privileged frame, so there is no unique objective 'now,' yet presentism holds that exactly one present moment is real, generating the conflict. Option 3 states a presentist-friendly conclusion (and is not what SR shows), while option 0 misdescribes SR; standard presentist replies posit a hidden privileged frame (neo-Lorentzian) or make the present frame-relative.
